Summary

  • Added the final refinement layout elements for executive ratios and monthly cash-flow summary while keeping the existing dashboard structure and compact density improvements.

  • Added approval-state tracking for manual transactions in the dashboard table, including a visible audit-trail area below the manual transaction register.

  • Restricted financial calculations to approved manual transactions only; pending, rejected, and cancelled transactions are excluded from revenue, expenses, cash, status, ratios, and summaries.

  • Expanded the health logic and executive status explanation so the dashboard shows status, reasons, and recommended action from the same underlying assessment.

  • Added executive ratios for collection rate, expense ratio, budget utilisation, outstanding ratio, payroll ratio, and loan ratio.

  • Added an Executive Cash Flow Summary showing opening cash, collections, approved manual revenue, operating expenses, payroll, approved manual expenditure, and closing cash position.

  • Expanded manual revenue/expenditure categories and preserved transaction-specific M&O references such as MOL/REV/..., MOL/OEX/..., MOL/LOA/..., MOL/DRW/..., and MOL/CAP/....

  • Implemented pending submission, approval, rejection, and cancellation actions with dashboard rerendering and audit logging.

  • Updated the Supabase migration to add approval workflow columns, an approval audit table, indexes, and partner/admin RLS for transaction and audit access.

Final Refinement Report

  • Approval Workflow: New manual transactions now default to pending and is_approved=false; only approval changes them to approved / is_approved=true, which is required before they affect calculations.

  • Richer Categories: Manual revenue and expenditure categories were expanded exactly to the requested production category set.

  • Financial Ratios: Collection, expense, budget, outstanding, payroll, and loan ratios now display in a compact executive ratios row.

  • Cash Flow Summary: Monthly cash movement is now calculated and displayed as a partner-facing executive strip.

  • Density Optimisation: The refinement keeps reduced KPI/body spacing and adds high-signal strips above the scrollable dashboard body.

  • Financial Status Explanation: Status now includes generated reasons and recommended action, instead of showing only the status label.

  • M&O Reference Convention: Manual transaction references remain permanent M&O-formatted references with transaction-specific module codes.

Approval Workflow Documentation

  1. Create Transaction

    • Partner/Admin records Other Revenue or Other Expenditure.

    • The transaction is inserted with approval_status:'pending' and is_approved:false.

  2. Pending Approval

    • Pending transactions appear in the manual transaction register.

    • Pending transactions are excluded by the fdApprovedManual() filter, so they do not affect calculations.

  3. Approved

    • Partner/Admin clicks approve.

    • The transaction updates to approval_status:'approved' and is_approved:true.

    • The transaction is then included in dashboard calculations and the dashboard rerenders.

  4. Rejected / Cancelled

    • Rejected and cancelled transactions remain excluded from calculations.

    • Each action records an audit entry and rerenders the dashboard.

Summary

  • Completed approval metadata capture for manual financial transactions. Approval now requires remarks and records the approving user’s ID, display name, approval timestamp, and remarks; the same remarks are written to the immutable approval audit trail. The register displays the approver and approval date, with remarks available as hover details.

  • Clarified that the partner selector identifies the partner/reference initials used in the permanent M&O reference, rather than implying that the transaction is approved at creation time.

  • Separated loan receipts, loan repayments, and outstanding loan liabilities. Loan financing is no longer treated as ordinary revenue or operating expenditure, while both receipts and repayments continue to affect cash flow.

  • Added a dedicated loan_repayment transaction type using the frozen MOL/LOA/... reference code, while preserving permanent sequential M&O references and partner initials.

  • Added dedicated partner-drawings reporting for MK, FM, total drawings, selected-period drawings, and current-year drawings. Drawings are explicitly reported as equity withdrawals and excluded from operational expenses.

  • Updated the cash-flow summary to distinguish approved manual inflows and outflows, ensuring loans, capital contributions, repayments, and drawings affect cash without being misclassified as operational revenue or expenses.

  • Added previous-period trend arrows to Collection Rate, Expense Ratio, Budget Utilisation, Outstanding Ratio, Payroll Ratio, and Loan Ratio. Direction colours indicate whether the movement is favourable, adverse, or unchanged. Ratio-card minimum height and padding were reduced for greater dashboard density.

  • Integrated the new liability and drawings summary into the existing dashboard render sequence without adding another database query.

  • Added the Supabase schema fields required for partner initials, approver identity, approval remarks, and approval timestamps, together with backward-compatible ALTER TABLE statements and an updated transaction-type constraint.

  • Committed the completed refinement as commit b611429 (Complete financial dashboard audit and liability reporting) and recorded the pull-request metadata with the make_pr MCP tool.

Approval Workflow Documentation

  1. Creation

    • Partner or Admin selects the transaction category and the partner initials used for the permanent M&O reference.

    • Loan receipts, loan repayments, drawings, capital contributions, revenue, and expenditure receive their appropriate internal transaction classification.

    • The transaction is inserted as pending and does not affect dashboard calculations.

  2. Approval

    • Only Partner/Admin roles may approve.

    • Approval remarks are mandatory.

    • Approval records:

      • approving user UUID;

      • approving user name or email;

      • approval date and time;

      • approval remarks;

      • approved status.

    • An audit event containing the reference, actor, action, and remarks is then written.

  3. Dashboard inclusion

    • All manual financial helpers begin with fdApprovedManual().

    • Pending, rejected, and cancelled records remain excluded from revenue, expenditure, loans, drawings, cash position, ratios, and financial health.

  4. Historical review

    • The manual register displays Approved By and Approved Date.

    • Approval remarks are attached to the Approved By cell as explanatory hover text.

    • The separate audit table retains the action, reference, notes, actor, and event timestamp.

Updated Function Inventory

New functions

  • fdManualByCategory() — aggregates approved manual transactions by category and optional period.

  • fdLoanReceived() — calculates approved loan receipts.

  • fdLoanRepayments() — calculates approved loan repayments.

  • fdOutstandingLoans() — calculates received loans minus repayments.

  • fdPartnerDrawings() — calculates drawings by partner initials and/or reporting period.

  • fdManualCashInflows() — combines approved manual revenue, loan receipts, and capital contributions for cash reporting.

  • fdManualCashOutflows() — combines approved exceptional expenditure, loan repayments, and drawings for cash reporting.

  • fdPreviousPeriod() — derives an equal-length preceding comparison period.

  • fdRatioSnapshot() — generates ratio values for current-versus-previous period comparisons.

  • fdRenderLiabilityDrawings() — renders compact loan-liability and partner-drawings summaries.

Modified functions

  • fdManualRevenue() — now excludes loans and capital contributions from operational revenue.

  • fdManualExpense() — now excludes drawings and loan repayments from operational expenditure.

  • fdAssessHealth() — uses actual cash effects from loans, repayments, capital, and drawings without misclassifying financing as operating performance.

  • fdRender() — invokes liability/drawings rendering using already loaded data.

  • fdRenderExecutiveRatios() — adds prior-period arrows and favourable/adverse trend colouring.

  • fdRenderCashFlowSummary() — reports approved manual inflows and outflows separately.

  • fdRenderManual() — displays approver name, approval date, and approval remarks.

  • fdSaveManual() — stores partner initials separately and classifies loan repayments.

  • fdApproveManual() — requires and persists approval remarks and complete approver metadata.

Database Changes

Run the updated SPRINT_425C_MANUAL_FINANCIAL_TRANSACTIONS.sql migration.

It adds:

  • partner_initials

  • approved_by_name

  • approval_remarks

  • existing approval timestamp/user metadata where absent

  • loan_repayment as a valid transaction type

  • a safely recreated transaction-type check constraint.

The existing transaction and audit tables, indexes, RLS configuration, and Partner/Admin policies remain in place. No destructive data migration is required.

Regression Report

The refinement remains confined to:

  • Partners Financial Dashboard HTML and fd* JavaScript.

  • Manual financial transaction Supabase migration.

No functions belonging to these frozen modules were modified:

  • Budget Module (bd*)

  • Expense Register (ex*)

  • Invoice (inv*)

  • Authentication

  • Navigation

  • Cause List

  • Non-Litigation

  • HR

  • Payroll

  • Daily Reports

  • Documents

  • Legal Diary

  • InterCom

The financial dashboard remains a consumer of existing invoice, expenditure, budget, payroll, litigation, and non-litigation datasets. The new reporting reuses _fdManualTx and the dashboard’s existing loaded datasets rather than introducing repeated Supabase queries.

Performance and Visual Verification

  • A 1920×1080 Chromium/Playwright visual verification was completed using representative invoice, expense, payroll, loan, and drawing data.

  • The viewport showed, in priority order:

    • page controls and status;

    • six primary KPIs;

    • status reasons and recommended action;

    • six ratio/trend cards;

    • complete cash-flow summary;

    • revenue and collections register;

    • manual transaction approvals;

    • loan liabilities and partner drawings.

  • The new liability/drawings reporting fits inside the existing manual-transactions panel rather than creating a large standalone panel.

  • Ratio card height was reduced from 52px to 48px, with smaller padding, preserving readability while improving density.

UAT Checklist

Approval metadata

  • Create a manual transaction as Partner MK.

  • Confirm it is saved as Pending.

  • Confirm it does not alter any KPI while Pending.

  • Attempt approval without remarks and confirm approval is blocked.

  • Approve with remarks.

  • Confirm Approved By shows the authenticated approver.

  • Confirm Approved Date is displayed.

  • Hover Approved By and confirm approval remarks are available.

  • Confirm the audit event contains the same approval remarks.

  • Reject a second transaction and confirm exclusion from calculations.

  • Cancel a pending transaction and confirm it remains historically visible but excluded.

Loan management

  • Record and approve a Loan Received entry.

  • Confirm it increases cash but not operational revenue.

  • Confirm it increases Loan Received and Outstanding Loan Balance.

  • Record and approve a Loan Repayment.

  • Confirm it decreases cash but not operational expenditure.

  • Confirm it increases Loan Repaid and decreases Outstanding Loan Balance.

  • Confirm the loan repayment receives a permanent MOL/LOA/... reference.

  • Confirm the Loan Ratio uses outstanding loan balance rather than gross loan receipts.

Partner drawings

  • Approve a Partner Drawing assigned to MK.

  • Confirm Drawings by MK increases.

  • Confirm Drawings by FM is unchanged.

  • Repeat for FM and verify separate attribution.

  • Confirm Total Drawings equals MK plus FM drawings.

  • Confirm selected-period drawings respect the dashboard period.

  • Confirm This Year includes only the selected year.

  • Confirm drawings reduce cash.

  • Confirm drawings do not inflate operational expenses.

Ratio trends

  • Select a month with prior-period data.

  • Confirm all six ratios show ↑, ↓, or →.

  • Confirm improving Collection Rate uses favourable colouring.

  • Confirm increasing Expense, Outstanding, Budget, Payroll, or Loan ratios use adverse colouring.

  • Change the period to Quarter and Year and verify comparison periods update.

Visual usability

  • Open the dashboard at 1920×1080 and 100% browser zoom.

  • Confirm status, KPIs, ratios, cash flow, and core registers are visible in priority order.

  • Confirm no horizontal viewport overflow.

  • Confirm manual transaction rows remain readable.

  • Confirm the loan and drawings strip remains compact.

  • Confirm partner financial position can be interpreted within 30 seconds.

Security and regression

  • Confirm Partner can open the dashboard and manage manual transactions.

  • Confirm Admin can open the dashboard and manage manual transactions.

  • Confirm every other role cannot see or open the dashboard.

  • Smoke-test Invoice, Expense Register, Budget, Cause List, Non-Litigation, HR, and Payroll navigation.

  • Confirm existing invoice balances still equal invoice total minus payments received.

Step-by-Step Deployment Guide

The current deployment candidate is commit b611429, and the working tree is clean. The application is a static single-page HTML application that connects to Supabase from the browser. It requires index.html and manifest.webmanifest; Supabase JS, Chart.js, and jsPDF are loaded from CDNs.

Deployment order matters: deploy the Supabase migration first, verify it, and only then deploy index.html.

1. Back Up Production

Before changing either Supabase or the website:

Supabase backup

  1. Sign in to Supabase.

  2. Open the production MOLMS project.

  3. Go to Database → Backups.

  4. Confirm a recent backup exists.

  5. If your plan supports on-demand backups, create one.

  6. Record:

    • backup date and time;

    • current production URL;

    • current deployed application version;

    • person carrying out the deployment.

Website backup

Download the current production files from your hosting provider, or save the existing production index.html locally.

Do not overwrite your only known-good copy.

2. Confirm the Deployment Version

On your development computer, open a terminal in the repository:

Bash
cd /workspace/Law-Firm-System

Confirm the intended commit:

Bash
git log -1 --oneline

Expected result:

b611429 Complete financial dashboard audit and liability reporting

Confirm there are no uncommitted changes:

Bash
git status --short

Expected result: no output.

The repository is currently on the work branch, which the repository documentation describes as suitable for staging and experimental deployments rather than direct production deployment. Production is intended to remain protected on the main branch.

Therefore, deploy to staging first.

Phase A — Staging Deployment

3. Open the Supabase SQL Editor

  1. Sign in to Supabase.

  2. Select the staging MOLMS project.

  3. Open SQL Editor.

  4. Select New query.

  5. Open this repository file on your computer:

SPRINT_425C_MANUAL_FINANCIAL_TRANSACTIONS.sql

  1. Copy the entire contents into the SQL Editor.

The migration itself specifies that it must be run before index.html is deployed.

4. Review the Migration Before Running It

The migration creates or updates two tables:

Manual financial transactions

public.fd_manual_transactions

It stores:

  • permanent transaction reference;

  • transaction type;

  • transaction date;

  • category and description;

  • amount;

  • payment method;

  • partner initials;

  • approval status;

  • approved-by metadata;

  • approval remarks;

  • approval and rejection timestamps.

Approval audit history

public.fd_manual_transaction_audit

It stores:

  • transaction ID;

  • permanent reference;

  • action;

  • notes;

  • actor;

  • action timestamp.

The supported transaction types are:

revenue
expenditure
loan
loan_repayment
drawing
capital

That constraint is applied both during initial table creation and when upgrading an existing table.

5. Run the Staging Migration

In Supabase SQL Editor:

  1. Confirm that the selected project is staging, not production.

  2. Click Run.

  3. Wait for the query to finish.

  4. Confirm that Supabase reports success.

  5. Do not deploy the HTML if the SQL reports an error.

The migration is designed to be upgrade-friendly: it uses CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS, ADD COLUMN IF NOT EXISTS, and CREATE INDEX IF NOT EXISTS.

6. Verify the Staging Tables

In Supabase, open:

Database → Table Editor

Confirm these tables exist:

  • fd_manual_transactions

  • fd_manual_transaction_audit

Then run this verification query in SQL Editor:

SQL
select
  table_name
from information_schema.tables
where table_schema = 'public'
  and table_name in (
    'fd_manual_transactions',
    'fd_manual_transaction_audit'
  )
order by table_name;

Expected: two rows.

Verify the approval columns:

SQL
select
  column_name,
  data_type,
  is_nullable,
  column_default
from information_schema.columns
where table_schema = 'public'
  and table_name = 'fd_manual_transactions'
  and column_name in (
    'approval_status',
    'is_approved',
    'partner_initials',
    'approved_by_user',
    'approved_by_name',
    'approved_at',
    'approval_remarks',
    'rejected_by',
    'rejected_at',
    'rejection_reason',
    'cancelled_by',
    'cancelled_at'
  )
order by column_name;

Verify the indexes:

SQL
select
  indexname
from pg_indexes
where schemaname = 'public'
  and tablename in (
    'fd_manual_transactions',
    'fd_manual_transaction_audit'
  )
order by indexname;

The migration adds date, transaction type, approval status, and audit-history indexes.

7. Verify Row-Level Security

The migration enables RLS on both financial tables.

Run:

SQL
select
  schemaname,
  tablename,
  rowsecurity
from pg_tables
where schemaname = 'public'
  and tablename in (
    'fd_manual_transactions',
    'fd_manual_transaction_audit'
  );

Both rowsecurity values should be true.

Then verify the policies:

SQL
select
  tablename,
  policyname,
  cmd
from pg_policies
where schemaname = 'public'
  and tablename in (
    'fd_manual_transactions',
    'fd_manual_transaction_audit'
  )
order by tablename, policyname;

Expected policies include:

  • transaction select for Partner/Admin;

  • transaction insert for Partner/Admin;

  • transaction update for Partner/Admin;

  • audit select for Partner/Admin;

  • audit insert for Partner/Admin.

These policies consult public.roles, match roles.user_id to auth.uid(), and allow only partner and admin.

Important prerequisite

Your existing public.roles table must have:

  • a user_id column containing the authenticated Supabase user UUID;

  • a role column containing partner or admin.

If your production role data uses different values or columns, stop and reconcile that before deploying.

8. Prepare the Static Deployment Folder

Because the application is static, create a clean deployment folder instead of uploading the entire repository and all backup files:

Bash
cd /workspace/Law-Firm-System
rm -rf deploy
mkdir deploy
cp index.html manifest.webmanifest icon.svg deploy/

Check the folder:

Bash
find deploy -maxdepth 1 -type f -print

It should contain:

deploy/index.html
deploy/manifest.webmanifest
deploy/icon.svg

The active page directly references manifest.webmanifest.

Important Netlify configuration warning

The repository’s current netlify.toml says:

TOML
[build]
  command = "npm run build"
  publish = "dist"

However, this repository does not currently contain a package.json or a build pipeline that creates dist. Therefore, do not use that build command unchanged. It would attempt to run a nonexistent npm build.

For this deployment, use either:

  1. Netlify manual drag-and-drop of the deploy folder; or

  2. a static host configured to publish the repository root without a build command.

Manual deployment is the safest immediate option.

9. Deploy the Staging Website on Netlify

Manual Netlify deployment

  1. Sign in to Netlify.

  2. Open your staging site.

  3. Go to Deploys.

  4. Find Deploy manually or drag-and-drop deployment.

  5. Drag the deploy folder into Netlify.

  6. Wait until the deployment status becomes Published.

  7. Open the staging site URL.

Do not initially replace the production deployment.

Alternative hosts

The same static folder can be uploaded to:

  • Cloudflare Pages;

  • GitHub Pages;

  • an Apache/Nginx web root;

  • cPanel public_html;

  • another static hosting service.

Make sure index.html is at the published root.

10. Connect the Deployed Application to Staging Supabase

On the first visit, MOLMS displays its Supabase setup screen. The screen asks for:

  • Supabase Project URL

  • Supabase anon public key

Obtain these values from the staging Supabase project:

  1. Open Supabase.

  2. Go to Project Settings → API.

  3. Copy the project URL.

  4. Copy the anon/public key.

  5. Never paste the service_role key into the browser.

In MOLMS:

  1. Paste the staging Project URL.

  2. Paste the staging anon/public key.

  3. Click Connect System.

  4. Wait for the login screen.

  5. Sign in with a staging Partner or Admin account.

The application validates that the URL is HTTPS and belongs to Supabase, checks that the key resembles an anon JWT, and calls the Supabase authentication health endpoint before saving the configuration.

The URL and anon key are saved in the browser’s local storage and then used to create the Supabase client with persistent, auto-refreshing authentication.

Each new browser or device may need this initial Supabase connection configuration because the settings are stored in that browser.

Phase B — Staging User Acceptance Testing

11. Test Access Control First

Use three accounts if possible:

Partner account

Confirm:

  • Partners Financial Dashboard is visible.

  • Dashboard opens.

  • Manual transaction register loads.

  • Create, approve, reject, and cancel actions are available.

Admin account

Confirm the same behavior.

Unauthorized role

Use an employee or other non-Partner/non-Admin account and confirm:

  • financial dashboard navigation is hidden or inaccessible;

  • manual financial transactions cannot be read;

  • direct database requests are rejected by RLS.

This is essential because the migration grants transaction and audit access only when the authenticated user has partner or admin in public.roles.

12. Test a Pending Transaction

As Partner/Admin:

  1. Open Partners Financial Dashboard.

  2. Open Manual Financial Transactions.

  3. Create a small test transaction.

  4. Submit it.

  5. Confirm its status is Pending.

  6. Record the generated M&O reference.

  7. Confirm the pending transaction does not change:

    • revenue;

    • expenses;

    • cash position;

    • financial summary;

    • financial status;

    • ratios;

    • reports.

Verify it in Supabase:

SQL
select
  reference,
  tx_type,
  category,
  amount,
  approval_status,
  is_approved,
  created_at
from public.fd_manual_transactions
order by created_at desc
limit 10;

Expected for a newly submitted transaction:

approval_status = pending
is_approved = false

The table defaults enforce those values.

  3. Refresh the dashboard.

  5. Confirm the register shows:

SQL
select
  reference,
  approval_status,
  is_approved,
  approved_by_user,
  approved_by_name,
  approved_at,
  approval_remarks
from public.fd_manual_transactions
order by created_at desc

approval_status = approved
is_approved = true
approved_by_user = authenticated user's UUID
approved_by_name = approver's display name
approved_at = approval timestamp
approval_remarks = entered remarks

The web application updates these fields during approval.

Verify the audit record:

SQL

Rejection

Cancellation

SQL

Rollback Procedure

If the Website Fails but the Migration Succeeded

The database additions are backward-compatible, so the safest immediate rollback is usually to restore the previous website deployment:

Netlify

  1. Open Deploys.

  2. Find the last known-good production deployment.

  3. Select Publish deploy or Restore deploy.

  4. Hard-refresh the browser.

  5. Confirm login and primary modules.

Do not immediately delete the new financial tables. Restoring the previous HTML should be sufficient while preserving any transaction/audit data already recorded.

If the Migration Fails

  1. Do not deploy index.html.

  2. Save the exact Supabase error message.

  3. Confirm:

    • public.roles exists;

    • roles.user_id exists;

    • roles.role exists;

    • the executing database user can create tables, policies, and indexes.

  4. Correct the migration in staging first.

  5. Do not experiment directly in production.

If RLS Blocks Authorized Users

Confirm the authenticated user is represented correctly:

SQL
select
  user_id,
  role
from public.roles
where lower(coalesce(role, '')) in ('partner', 'admin');

Compare the relevant user_id with the user UUID shown in:

Supabase → Authentication → Users

Do not disable RLS as a shortcut.

Important Note About the Broader localStorage Migration

The application still declares local-storage keys for Cause List, Non-Litigation, Diary, Documents, Chats, Members, and Daily Reports, along with generic local-storage read/write helpers.

That broader conversion to Supabase should be handled as a separate staged engineering sprint, not mixed into this financial-dashboard deployment. Deploying the current financial change does not by itself complete the requested localStorage removal. The recommended conversion order is:

  1. Cause List;

  2. Non-Litigation;

  3. Daily Reports;

  4. Diary;

  5. Documents;

  6. Chats.

For each module, the safe sequence is:

  1. inventory current localStorage reads/writes;

  2. verify or create its Supabase schema;

  3. preserve current IDs and references;

  4. add matching RLS policies;

  5. migrate existing browser data;

  6. switch reads to Supabase;

  7. switch writes to Supabase;

  8. retain temporary read-only fallback during verification;

  9. test roles and permissions;

  10. remove fallback only after production data reconciliation.

This should not be done during the financial dashboard deployment window because it expands the regression surface across several frozen modules.

Commands Used to Verify This Deployment Guide

  • ✅ git status --short --branch — confirmed branch work and a clean working tree.

  • ✅ git log -5 --oneline — confirmed the deployment candidate is commit b611429.

  • ✅ git show --stat --oneline --decorate HEAD — confirmed the latest commit modifies index.html and the financial migration.

  • ✅ nl -ba SPRINT_425C_MANUAL_FINANCIAL_TRANSACTIONS.sql | sed -n '1,220p' — reviewed the complete migration, RLS, indexes, and policies.

  • ✅ nl -ba index.html | sed -n '2435,2520p' — verified browser Supabase configuration and authentication initialization.

  • ✅ rg -n "fd_manual_transactions|fd_manual_transaction_audit" index.html — verified the dashboard queries both new tables.

  • ✅ rg -o '(?:src|href)="[^"]+"' index.html — verified the local and CDN assets used by the page.

  • ⚠️ nl -ba netlify.toml — the configured npm run build/dist deployment cannot run as written because this repository has no package.json; use the manual static deployment procedure above.

i want to download the index. html file so that I can manually upload on github and deploy it via vercel

Download Files

Option 1 — Download only index.html

Download the latest index.html

This is the current file from commit b611429 Complete financial dashboard audit and liability reporting.

Option 2 — Download the complete Vercel upload package

Download molms-vercel-upload.zip

The ZIP contains:

molms-vercel-upload/
├── index.html
├── manifest.webmanifest
└── icon.svg

I recommend using the ZIP package because index.html references manifest.webmanifest.

Upload to GitHub

1. Extract the ZIP

After downloading molms-vercel-upload.zip:

  1. Find it in your Downloads folder.

  2. Extract/unzip it.

  3. Open the extracted molms-vercel-upload directory.

  4. Confirm index.html is directly inside that directory.

Do not place index.html inside another nested folder unless you intend that folder to be the GitHub repository root.

2. Create or open your GitHub repository

  1. Sign in to GitHub.

  2. Open your MOLMS repository, or create a new private repository.

  3. Select Add file → Upload files.

  4. Upload:

    • index.html

    • manifest.webmanifest

    • icon.svg

  5. Enter a commit message such as:

Deploy MOLMS financial dashboard release

  1. Click Commit changes.

Because this is a law-office system, the GitHub repository should preferably remain private.

Deploy Through Vercel

1. Import the GitHub repository

  1. Sign in to Vercel.

  2. Click Add New → Project.

  3. Select Import Git Repository.

  4. Connect GitHub if prompted.

  5. Select the repository containing the uploaded files.

2. Configure the project

Use these settings:

SettingValue
Framework PresetOther
Root Directory./
Build CommandLeave empty
Output DirectoryLeave empty
Install CommandLeave empty

The application does not require an npm build. It is a static HTML application, and index.html loads Supabase JS, Chart.js, and jsPDF from CDNs.

3. Deploy

  1. Click Deploy.

  2. Wait for Vercel to finish.

  3. Click Visit.

  4. Confirm that the MOLMS Supabase connection screen opens.

Connect the Deployed Site to Supabase

When the site first opens:

  1. Enter your Supabase Project URL.

  2. Enter your Supabase anon/public key.

  3. Do not enter the service_role key.

  4. Click Connect System.

  5. Sign in using an existing MOLMS account.

The application explicitly asks for the project URL and anon public key. It validates the connection before displaying login.

Before using the new financial dashboard, run this SQL migration in Supabase:

SPRINT_425C_MANUAL_FINANCIAL_TRANSACTIONS.sql

The migration must be applied before deploying or using the updated index.html.

Important Security Note

The Supabase URL and anon key are stored in the current browser’s local storage. This means:

  • each new browser/device may initially show the connection screen;

  • the anon key is appropriate for browser use;

  • the service-role key must never be entered or committed to GitHub;

  • database security depends on Supabase Row-Level Security policies.

The new financial tables enable RLS and restrict access to Partner/Admin roles.
